items.front: Babur's descent and the battle that founded Mughal rule?
items.back: Descendant of Timur (paternal) & Genghis Khan (maternal); First Panipat (1526) vs Ibrahim Lodi.
items.examPoint: First Battle of Panipat (1526) — Babur vs Ibrahim Lodi; artillery & tulughma

items.front: Babur's four decisive battles in order?
items.back: Panipat (1526), Khanwa (1527, vs Rana Sanga), Chanderi (1528), Ghaghra (1529).
items.examPoint: Battle of Khanwa (1527) — Babur vs Rana Sanga

items.front: In what language did Babur write his memoirs, and what are they called?
Two battles Humayun lost to Sher Shah, and when he was restored?
items.examPoint: Battles of Chausa (1539) & Kannauj/Bilgram (1540); exile & 1555 restoration

items.front: Sher Shah Suri's economic and road reforms?
items.back: Silver rupiya & copper dam; revived the Grand Trunk Road with sarais; used dagh & chehra.
items.examPoint: Sher Shah's economy — silver rupiya, Grand Trunk Road, sarais, dagh & chehra

items.back: Sarkar/pargana units, land measured, one-third of produce; peasants got patta & kabuliyat.
items.examPoint: Sher Shah's land-revenue reforms (patta, kabuliyat, sarkar/pargana)

items.front: Who won the Second Battle of Panipat (1556) for Akbar, and against whom?
items.back: Bairam Khan (regent) against Hemu; Akbar had just acceded aged 13.
items.examPoint: Akbar's accession (1556), Bairam Khan & Second Battle of Panipat (Hemu)

items.back: Abolished jizya (1564), promoted Sulh-i-Kul (Ibadat Khana debates), founded Din-i-Ilahi (1582).
items.examPoint: Akbar's religious policy — jizya abolition, Sulh-i-Kul, Din-i-Ilahi

items.front: Akbar's revenue system, and who implemented it?
items.back: Dahsala/Zabti (Todar Mal's Bandobast) — revenue on 10-year average produce/prices; state share one-third.

items.front: What do Zat and Sawar mean in the Mansabdari system?
items.back: Zat = personal rank/status/pay; Sawar = number of cavalry a mansabdar must maintain.

items.front: Who wrote the Akbarnama, and what is its third volume?
items.back: Abul Fazl; its third volume is the Ain-i-Akbari. He was one of Akbar's Navaratnas.

items.front: Which English envoy came to Jahangir, and where was the first factory?
items.back: Sir Thomas Roe (envoy of James I); first English factory at Surat (1613). Jahangir married Nur Jahan.
items.examPoint: Jahangir — Nur Jahan, chain of justice, Sir Thomas Roe & Surat factory

items.front: Shah Jahan's signature monuments and throne?
items.back: Taj Mahal (for Mumtaz Mahal), Red Fort, Jama Masjid; the jewelled Peacock Throne (Takht-i-Taus).
items.examPoint: Shah Jahan — Taj Mahal, peak Mughal architecture, Peacock Throne

items.front: Aurangzeb — jizya year, and the two Deccan sultanates he annexed?
items.back: Re-imposed jizya in 1679; annexed Bijapur (1686) and Golconda (1687).
items.examPoint: Aurangzeb — war of succession, jizya (1679), Deccan & Bijapur-Golconda

items.front: Who sacked Delhi in 1739; and who beat the Marathas at Panipat 1761?
items.back: Nadir Shah (1739, took Peacock Throne & Koh-i-Noor); Ahmad Shah Abdali at Third Panipat (1761).
items.examPoint: Later Mughals & decline — Nadir Shah (1739), Ahmad Shah Abdali, Bahadur Shah II
